meta.description: Plain-language definitions of common cybercrime and online-safety terms, complementing our safety tips.

title: Cyber Awareness
subtitle: Short, plain-language definitions for terms you'll see in advisories, news, and scam warnings. For what to actually do, see our Cyber Safety Tips.

terms.title: Phishing
terms.body: A fake email or message designed to look like it's from a real organisation, aimed at tricking you into revealing a password, OTP, or card details.

terms.title: Vishing
terms.body: The same trick as phishing, done over a phone call instead of a message, often by someone pretending to be from your bank or the police.

terms.title: Smishing
terms.body: Phishing sent by SMS, usually a short, urgent message with a link, about a parcel, a KYC update, or a blocked account.

terms.title: Malware
terms.body: Software installed on your device without your informed consent that can steal data, spy on you, or damage your device. Often arrives disguised as a useful app.

terms.title: Ransomware
terms.body: Malware that locks or encrypts your files and demands payment to unlock them. Paying does not guarantee your files come back.

terms.title: Identity theft
terms.body: Someone using your personal details, like your name, Aadhaar, or PAN, to open accounts, take loans, or commit fraud in your name without your knowledge.

terms.title: Two-factor authentication (2FA)
terms.body: A second proof of identity, beyond your password, needed to log in, usually an OTP or an authenticator app. Turning it on for email and banking apps makes a stolen password far less useful to an attacker.

terms.title: Digital footprint
terms.body: The trail of data you leave behind through what you post, search, and share online. Scammers often use publicly visible details from it to make a fake call sound convincing.

terms.title: Digital arrest scam
terms.body: A specific vishing pattern where a caller impersonates law enforcement and claims you're under "digital arrest," pressuring you to stay on a call and pay money. No real Indian agency arrests anyone this way.

terms.title: Sextortion
terms.body: Blackmail where someone threatens to share private or fabricated intimate images or videos unless you pay them or send more content.

footer: Knowing the terms helps you recognise a pattern faster. For the actions to take before and after something happens, see our <link>Cyber Safety Tips</link>.
